subject.title: [Refactor] Abstract OAuth flow parameters out of LLM transport core

question: Should provider OAuth flow parameters remain entirely provider-plugin owned, or should OpenClaw add a new generic injectable contract after the reporter identifies a concrete provider blocked by current hooks?
rationale: Source and docs show existing provider and transport-host seams, but the report provides too little concrete behavior to determine whether a new permanent API is necessary or duplicative.

options.title: Require a concrete missing seam
options.body: Keep the provider-owned architecture and ask for the exact literals, caller, blocked provider, and why current hooks cannot express the behavior before designing an API.

options.title: Design a generic OAuth contract
options.body: Sponsor a compatibility-sensitive `@openclaw/ai` or plugin-SDK API now and define its ownership, lifecycle, and migration contract before implementation.

options.title: Treat current hooks as sufficient
options.body: Close the request if maintainers confirm that provider registration and `AiTransportHost` injection already cover every intended use case.

recommendation.title: Require a concrete missing seam
recommendation.body: Keep the provider-owned architecture and ask for the exact literals, caller, blocked provider, and why current hooks cannot express the behavior before designing an API.

likelyOwner.reason: The question determines a permanent core-versus-provider API boundary and steipete is the strongest documented architecture owner.
